tests.name: backup taken while a writer is running restores to a consistent committed prefix with sources, ACLs, tombstones and profiles intact
torn or corrupted backups are refused, never restored as if healthy
purge: removes content from the live vault; a pre-purge backup still holds it (documented retention limit)
manifest-checked backups: complete ones restore; missing manifest, extra files, edits and a backup killed mid-copy are all refused

gaps.reason: Restores go to a fresh directory on the same host.
A backup taken before a purge keeps the plaintext. This is tested and documented, not solved.
Restore wall time is measured on a small vault; no cadence is defined or scheduled.
Backups are full copies under the writer lock.

limitations: Backups hold the writer lock, so a backup during writes is a consistent point but delays writers.
A same-disk revision history is not a backup.

detail.rpoNote: RPO = time since last backup; RTO = restore wall time above (small vault).
